clue.text: He dealt with state affairs a lot — wrong description of Boris?

definitions.note: Boris Johnson has six acknowledged children and has declined to confirm the total, hence the question mark

indicators.note: cards dealt are shuffled and spread out, so these clue words are rearranged

parts.note: a cross is the mark a teacher puts beside a wrong answer

explanation.surface: A politician who handled the nation's business, and had plenty of extramarital affairs too, is summed up in a phrase about Boris Johnson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affairs' tempts as romance and 'dealt with' as handled; it is the anagram signal on HE STATE AFFAIRS A LOT, with X for 'wrong' added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Johnson, former UK Prime Minister, has at least six children, so the phrase counting his offspring describes him.

clue.text: American star wearing nothing upstaged by a furry animal

indicators.note: to be upstaged is to have your place taken by another performer, so one piece is replaced by the letter A

parts.note: Al Pacino is an American film actor
wearing gives IN and nothing gives O, a zero

explanation.surface: A Hollywood actor appearing naked finds the attention stolen from him by a woolly creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing nothing' looks like nudity but supplies IN plus O, which the A replaces at the end of AL PACINO.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a South American relative of the llama prized for its soft woolly fleece.

clue.text: Red colour largely visible amongst evidence of fire

indicators.note: seen in the middle of something, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: ash is what is left after burning

indicators.note: most of the word but not all, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: blue is a colour

explanation.surface: A red tint can mostly be made out among the remains of a blaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' looks like a colour adjective to pair with 'colour', but it is the definition; 'largely' drops the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone flushed pink with embarrassment is red in the face, the sense of this adjective.

clue.text: Jailed German boy, cunning little pest

parts.note: Rudolf Hess, Nazi deputy, spent his last decades imprisoned in Spandau
Ian is a boy's name
fly is British slang for sharp or crafty

explanation.surface: A German lad has been locked up for being a sly little troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Fly meaning cunning is informal British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: This small gall midge is a serious insect enemy of wheat crops, so it is a little pest.

clue.text: Head of state is stock market malefactor? No way!

indicators.note: with no way, the street abbreviation is removed from the word

parts.note: a rustler steals livestock, which might be taken to market; the question mark flags the play on the financial sense
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Could a national leader be a crook on the stock exchange? Certainly not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock market' suggests finance, but the stock here is cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch or other sovereign governs a country, making them its head.

clue.text: Gridlock on motorway going west — go east

indicators.note: in an across answer, westward is right to left, so the motorway's letters run backwards

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north–south motorway, written MI
to pass is to have a go, as in a game turn
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Stuck in traffic on the motorway heading one way, a driver is told to go the other.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a British motorway; reversed it gives IM. 'Go' is a turn, as in passing in a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock or standstill where no progress is possible, as in jammed traffic or stalled talks.

clue.text: Wish to travel? Minimal cost when cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter round from one end to the other, here the front letter to the back

parts.note: titchy is British slang for tiny
a fee is a charge or cost

explanation.surface: A traveller longing to roam notices how little a bike trip costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when cycling' moves the T of TITCHY FEE from the front to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom describes restlessness, an urge to go somewhere new; the question mark covers the phrase's figurative feet.

clue.text: Phil's number one cut — that was close!

indicators.note: the first in line, so the first letter of the name is taken

parts.note: to hew is to chop or cut

explanation.surface: Phil's best one has been axed, and it was a narrow escape.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of relief after a near miss.

clue.text: Lively and encouraging, though not winning

indicators.note: the second piece is excluded from the first

parts.note: supportive means encouraging
up means ahead or winning, as in two goals up

explanation.surface: A sports fan is cheerful and backs the team even when it is losing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' as in being ahead in a game is removed from SUPPORTIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Frolicsome and playful, a lively temperament.

clue.text: Tragically timeless in role set here

definitions.note: the clue refers to its own subject: the place where a role in a tragedy is set

indicators.note: the letters are wrecked, with a nod to the tragedy whose setting this is
timeless means without T, the abbreviation for time, so that letter comes out of the word set

explanation.surface: Playing a tragic part, an actor's sense of timing fails in the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' removes T (time) from 'set'; 'Tragically' then rearranges IN ROLE SE. 'Here' points back to the clue's tragic role, Hamlet's.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danish castle at Helsingør is where Shakespeare sets Hamlet, a tragic role.

clue.text: Rudeness reciprocated leads to extremely serious complaint

indicators.note: reciprocated means given back, so the word for rudeness runs backwards

parts.note: lip is cheek, impudent talk

indicators.note: leads are the front letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: Rude words traded back and forth escalate into a grave grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' reads as a grievance; here it is a medical complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Haemorrhoids are an uncomfortable medical ailment, and complaint means ailment.

clue.text: Clue's naughty about great man having a roving eye

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the other piece
naughty means misbehaving, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a hero is a great man

explanation.surface: A cheeky crossword clue alludes to a celebrated man known for flirting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' rearranges CLUES into LEC...US, which goes 'about' HERO.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with a roving eye looks lustfully at others, which is lewd and lustful behaviour.

clue.text: Big Mike trapped by scary alien space travellers

indicators.note: one piece is held within the other
alien means strange, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize
a mic, or mike, is a microphone

explanation.surface: Large Mike has been captured by a frightening extraterrestrial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big' gives OS, outsize as on clothing labels; 'alien' signals the anagram rather than describing a visitor from space.
explanation.definitionFit: High-energy particles from outer space streaking through the cosmos are literally travellers through space.

clue.text: One repeatedly fired from EastEnders

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the name

explanation.surface: A character keeps getting sacked from the BBC soap EastEnders.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a long-running British TV soap opera. 'Fired' means sacked in the surface but shot here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sten was a British submachine gun of the Second World War, a weapon shooting bursts of bullets.

clue.text: Ships they're scrapping about to be saved

indicators.note: something saved is kept safe inside, so the short word goes within the longer

parts.note: people scrapping are fighting, so they are fighters
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Vessels are being broken up, but they are about to be rescued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrapping' suggests ships for scrap; it means fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo vessels carry goods, a kind of ship.

clue.text: Needing breaks? Could be Amazon job on the line

definitions.note: names the role by the person who does it, a railway worker

indicators.note: a word that breaks is broken up, its letters rearranged

parts.note: the Amazon is a South American river; 'Could be' flags it as an example

explanation.surface: Needing time off, a worker with the online retailer Amazon finds their job at risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amazon' suggests the retailer and 'on the line' a job at risk, but it is the river and a railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A train operator, the worker who drives a locomotive on the railway line.

clue.text: I catch visiting duke inside — pretty sick

parts.note: to nab is to catch

indicators.note: the duke's letter is put within the word for visiting

parts.note: a visiting team plays away

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have caught a visiting nobleman indoors while feeling unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Visiting' gives AWAY, as a sports team plays away from home.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom describes someone quite unwell, in poor health.

clue.text: Saw in here money raised by cast?

definitions.note: a saw is kept in this garden building

indicators.note: in a down answer, raising writes the word from bottom to top

parts.note: loot is slang for money
to cast is to shed, as a snake does its skin

explanation.surface: Someone noticed cash in here, collected by a theatre cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' reads as the past of see; it is the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden hut for storing implements is where a saw would be kept.

clue.text: Current unwelcome visitor camped in compound

indicators.note: compounded letters are mixed together into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An unwanted guest has set up camp in a walled enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' reads as an enclosure but signals mixing. The puzzle appeared in November 2020, during Covid.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease outbreak spreading worldwide arrives uninvited; when published, Covid-19 was very much present.

clue.text: See 1
Relatively famous broadcaster

parts.note: the BBC's affectionate nickname is a family relation, a parent's sister

explanation.surface: A moderately well-known presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relatively' seems to mean moderately but points to a relative: the BBC is nicknamed after one.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC, Britain's public broadcaster, is fondly nicknamed after a family relative.

clue.text: Coastal road (some might say) is capital

indicators.note: it is how some people would pronounce it, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: a bay route is a road along the coast

explanation.surface: A road along the shore is described, by some, as excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' seems to be the old British word for excellent; it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Lebanon's seat of government is this Mediterranean port city.

clue.text: Very short, my youngsters

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so a letter is missing

parts.note: from the setter's point of view, my means Vlad's, the setter's pseudonym

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that their children are quite small.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is Vlad, so 'my' gives VLAD'S, which, short of V for very, leaves the boys.
explanation.definitionFit: Boys or young men are youngsters.

clue.text: Weird — say, who'd be taking you inside old knocking shop?

definitions.note: knocking shop is British slang for a brothel; old because the term is dated

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it, so one piece contains another
inside places the letter for you within the scrambled letters
weird means strange, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: An odd remark about who would be taking you into a disreputable old establishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like a link to an example but is anagram fodder; U is the text-speak spelling of you.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated term for a brothel, a place of lewd goings-on.

clue.text: Senior member makes the same money

parts.note: do, short for ditto, means the same again
the yen is Japan's currency

explanation.surface: An elder colleague earns the same pay.
explanation.definitionFit: The most respected or longest-serving member of a group, its senior figure.

clue.text: Old Testament fellow (one getting leg over)

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means placed above

parts.note: the leg side in cricket is also called the on side
an means one

explanation.surface: A biblical character described as having sex, a cheeky aside.
explanation.walkthrough: Leg and on are the same side of a cricket field. 'Getting leg over', British slang for sex, is a nod to the figure's notoriety.
explanation.definitionFit: A son of Judah in Genesis, who spilled his seed rather than father children.

clue.text: Writer's block getting worse? Initially, yes

definitions.note: the definition is the writer; the 's stands for is, linking to the wordplay

parts.note: to hem in is to block or hedge

indicators.note: the starting letters of the two preceding words

parts.note: ay is an old or dialect word for yes

explanation.surface: Is a writer's creative blockage getting worse? At first, yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's block' looks like a phrase, but the writer is the definition and block the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest, American novelist of The Old Man and the Sea, a famous author.

clue.text: Tenant doesn't have right key

indicators.note: the letter for right is missing from the word

parts.note: a renter pays rent, as a tenant

explanation.surface: A renter lacks the correct key for the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' suggests a door key; it is the keyboard key.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard button for input, the return key on a computer.

clue.text: City in retreat — Coventry wingers showing good form

indicators.note: one piece is placed within another

parts.note: a den is a private retreat
EC is the postal district of the City of London

indicators.note: the outside players in a team, so the outside letters of the word

explanation.surface: Coventry City's wide players are on good form during a retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: Coventry City is a football club, so 'City' and 'wingers' seem football talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Propriety, behaving with good manners: good form in its social sense.

clue.text: Name going up in the early stages

definitions.note: an adjective phrase, matching this adjective

parts.note: an ascent is a going up

explanation.surface: A name is climbing in the early phases.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerging or just beginning to develop, just coming into being.
